DESCRIPTION: `novelty_rate` is computed over the already-filtered `new_findings_flat`, not over all findings from the round. In `process_round()`, the manager passes only members of `ConvergenceDetector._novel_classes(round_idx)` into `DiminishingReturnsDetector.add_round_from_findings()`. Then `add_round_from_findings()` divides `novel_count` by `len(new_findings)`. That makes duplicate churn invisible to the new stop signal. I reproduced a round containing one duplicate and one genuinely new finding; the detector reported `novelty_rate(1) == 1.0` instead of `0.5`, because the duplicate never entered the denominator.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute novelty rate against the full round finding set, or pass both `all_findings_this_round` and `novel_findings_this_round` into the diminishing-returns layer so the denominator reflects the actual round output.

DESCRIPTION: The new “immune response” layer is operationally inert. `DetectorHealthMonitor` says the manager decides whether to act, and it even exposes `has_critical`, but `DynamicManager.process_round()` only converts diagnoses into extra `STOP_CHECK` events and then proceeds with the normal FSM transition path. I verified this by forcing a `CRITICAL` diagnosis; the manager still advanced normally to `SYNTH` and did not abort, veto stopping, or change allocation logic.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Decide an explicit contract for CRITICAL diagnoses and wire it into control flow, for example: veto `DIMINISHED`, force a safe hold state, or mark the round result as diagnostically invalid until the detector issue is addressed.

DESCRIPTION: The health monitor’s “kappa stuck at 0.0 means similarity too strict” diagnosis is not identifiable from the data it receives. It only sees collapsed `kappa`, not `kappa_set`, `kappa_rate`, or `kappa_adopt`, so it can blame `_finding_similarity()` when the real cause is somewhere else. I reproduced repeated identical findings with `adoption_delta=1.0`; on round 2, `kappa_set(2) == 1.0` and duplicate detection was clearly working, but `kappa_adopt(2) == 0.0` drove combined `kappa` to `0.0`, and the health monitor still emitted “Similarity function may be too strict”.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Feed the health monitor the component metrics, not just combined `kappa`, and only attribute low `kappa` to similarity failure when `kappa_set` specifically is pathological.

DESCRIPTION: The novelty-based stop path treats total silence as evidence of exhaustion. When `new_findings` is empty, `add_round_from_findings()` stores `novelty_rate = 0.0`; after `r_min`, `stop()` returns true because `smoothed_novelty < tau_novelty_stop`, even if the system has simply seen no findings at all. I reproduced three empty rounds and got `novelty = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]`, `mu = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]`, `stop(2) == True`. That is the diminishing-returns analogue of the earlier “silence counts as success” bug.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Gate novelty-based stopping on positive evidence, for example require some minimum finding volume or an explicit `null_expected` flag before empty rounds can count as exhaustion.

DESCRIPTION: Similarity semantics are split across subsystems. `ConvergenceDetector` supports an injected `similarity_fn`, but the new novelty-rate path and fingerprint duplicate-rate path both hard-code `_finding_similarity`. I verified the divergence with a custom `similarity_fn=lambda *_: 1.0`: convergence reported round-1 novelty as zero, while `DiminishingReturnsDetector.novelty_rate(1)` still returned `1.0` because it ignored the injected comparator. This means convergence, diminishing-returns, and adaptive fingerprint updates can disagree about what “duplicate” means.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Centralize similarity behind one shared strategy object and pass it into all subsystems that reason about novelty or duplication, including fingerprint updates.
